observation_reviews.rationale: Independent original context has SOFR(Q), while its NFP row prints SOFR(M). Published SOFR loses tenor, so this is metadata disagreement rather than proof of a wrong stored benchmark. Proposed context-to-row tenor comparison catches recurrence if it flags only explicit comparable tenors and preserves source provenance; it must not auto-correct from the member or conflate benchmark family with tenor.

Independent Grinding Media context says 8.58/SOFR(M), while tagged numeric coupon is 7.83 and tagged benchmark enumeration ThreeMonths matches printed SOFR(Q). Polaris 2025-12-31 context says 8.85/4.00 while original facts and row say 7.85/3.75. Published values follow numeric facts. Proposed comparison is useful as a provenance flag; compare all-in coupon with all-in coupon and cash/PIK components separately with numeric tolerance, not as an automatic canonical-error gate. This avoids valid rate conventions producing false positives.
